clue.text: Point of view from Mail following comment

indicators.note: following tells us the mail word comes after the comment word

parts.note: a comment is an observation, a remark made
mail is post, letters delivered

explanation.surface: Someone forms an opinion from what the newspaper Mail says after a remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point of view' looks like an opinion, but it is a literal place to view from; 'from' is a link. The Mail is also a British newspaper, which helps the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A military lookout spot is literally a point from which one views the surroundings.

clue.text: Choose one degree student — the best!

parts.note: to choose is to opt
one is the Roman numeral I
MA is a Master of Arts degree
L is a learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A student is told to choose a single degree course because it is the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal is a synonym of best, the most favourable possible.

clue.text: Partners covering court pass out

indicators.note: covering means the partner letters sit around the court word

parts.note: in bridge, South and North are partners
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: Tennis doubles partners occupy the court and then collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: S and N are a bridge partnership; 'court' looks like a tennis court but is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon is to faint, which is to lose consciousness briefly.

clue.text: Looks like Bessemer process swallowed last of capital

indicators.note: swallowed means one piece is taken inside the other
to process something is to work it over, so the letters are reworked
last of picks the final letter of the word capital

explanation.surface: Industrial history: the Bessemer steel process ate up the remaining money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' rearranges BESSEMER into RESEMBES, which 'swallowed' wraps round L, the last letter of 'capital'. The Bessemer process is a historic steel-making method, hence the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To resemble something is to look like it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A single call should start getting public broadcasts

parts.note: single means one, the Roman numeral I
to call on the phone is to give a ring

indicators.note: start takes the opening letter of the word should

explanation.surface: Advice that a lone phone call ought to begin attracting media coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Airings are transmissions on radio or television, programmes put out to the public.

clue.text: Popular island group oddly scours for something with bite

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
CI stands for the Channel Islands

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of scours

explanation.surface: A trendy archipelago is scrubbed in odd fashion by a biting creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie off the French coast but belong to the British Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is a front cutting tooth, used to bite into food.

clue.text: Shortly returned bearing rope

indicators.note: returned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: shortly means soon, before long
E is a compass bearing, east

explanation.surface: Someone comes back soon carrying a length of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a looped rope, so the rope stands for the loop made from it.

clue.text: Worker's work time — time given without limits

definitions.note: read as 'worker is', the 's joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: without limits removes the first and last letters of the word given

explanation.surface: A labourer's shift is given with no fixed hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without limits' strips G and N from 'given', leaving IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially a factory hand or secret agent.

clue.text: People giving money for supplying trucks

definitions.meaning: those who leave a gratuity for service
lorries with a body that tilts to dump a load

explanation.definitionFit: A tipper is both someone who gives gratuities and a dumper lorry that tips its load out.

clue.text: Pocket found in short pants

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: pants in American usage are trousers

explanation.surface: A pocket is discovered in a pair of short trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocket' looks like a noun but is the verb to pocket, to take; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is British slang for pocketing it, usually dishonestly.

clue.text: Picture that will fail in competition

indicators.note: in places the failing word inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition
to lose is to fail to win

explanation.surface: A photograph of the team that is going to be knocked out of the tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that will' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a photograph or film shot taken from very near the subject.

clue.text: Times covers rumour of new memorials

indicators.note: covers means the times word goes round the other piece

parts.note: moments are short times

indicators.note: rumour of means what is heard said, so the word new is taken by sound

parts.note: new is said aloud and spelt NU

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper reports gossip about fresh memorials.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is a British newspaper, so the surface reads as press gossip; here 'Times' is just periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Monuments are statues or structures put up as memorials to people or events.

clue.text: Scrub for ages before finishing

parts.note: eras are ages, long periods

indicators.note: finishing takes the closing letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Cleaning for ages until the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a position word but supplies its last letter E; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or delete, as to scrub something from a record.

clue.text: Pubs full of energy are places where things happen

indicators.note: full of means the energy letter goes inside the pubs word

parts.note: a local is a person's nearby pub
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Lively pubs are where the action is.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOCAL is British for one's neighbourhood pub; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Locales are settings or scenes, the sites where events take place.

clue.text: Metal cutter is able to bat

parts.note: can means is able to
in cricket an opener is a batsman who opens the innings

explanation.surface: A piece of metalwork machinery that can be used to hit balls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers are the first two batsmen to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A can-opener cuts through the metal lid of a tin, so it is a cutter of metal.

clue.text: Makes good case for reliable couples

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: couples are pairs

explanation.surface: Someone argues the merits of dependable married couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for' takes the first and last letters of 'reliable', R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to mend it, to make good the damage.

clue.text: Deport all involved having done guard duty

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone caught up in deportation had served as guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges the letters of 'Deport all'.
explanation.definitionFit: To patrol is to keep watch over an area, which is guard duty.

clue.text: Drink following worker's surrender

indicators.note: following means the drink word comes after the worker word

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand; the 's adds no letters
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A labourer drinks and then gives in.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising one's arms is the gesture of surrender, so the call to raise them means give up.

clue.text: Panama protects a part of the environment

indicators.note: protects means the hat word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a Panama is a straw hat
a part means a bit

explanation.surface: The country of Panama safeguards a section of its ecology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' looks like the country but is the hat; 'of the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural surroundings in which a creature lives.

clue.text: Craft shop's last one — turn back in regret

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of shop's, ignoring the possessive

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the regret word

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in a game

explanation.surface: In a boat shop, someone regrets turning back the last item.
explanation.walkthrough: A pirogue is a dugout canoe; 'Craft' looks like skill or cunning but means a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a dugout canoe, a small boat or craft.

clue.text: Source of infection in obvious hospital case

indicators.note: in places the source letter inside the obvious word

parts.note: patent means obvious, plain to see

indicators.note: source of takes the opening letter of infection

explanation.surface: The origin of an infection is plain in a medical case.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient is someone being treated in hospital, a medical case.

clue.text: Very hot, absorbing pressure and beating

indicators.note: absorbing means the hot word takes the pressure letter inside

parts.note: piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: Something scalding takes in pressure and pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: PIPING goes with hot in the phrase 'piping hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pip someone is to beat them narrowly, as in pipping at the post.

clue.text: Altered setting of foot pedal

indicators.note: a new setting of the letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A modified foot pedal is fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder; 'setting of' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a lever worked by the foot, as on an old sewing machine.

clue.text: One quietly lying in the bottom of the sea? You!

indicators.note: lying in means these letters lie inside the sea-bottom word

parts.note: the seabed is the bottom of the sea
one is the Roman numeral I
p, piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone lying silently on the seabed: a question addressed to the reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the reader: you are a two-legged creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A human reader walks on two legs, so the solver is a two-legged animal.

clue.text: Urge that's mostly utter nonsense

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: drivel is utter nonsense

explanation.surface: A compulsion that is largely rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is a strong motivating urge, as in sex drive or ambition.

clue.text: Refund accepted on behalf of wastrel

indicators.note: accepted means the refund word takes the other piece inside

parts.note: a rebate is a partial refund
pro means for, on behalf of

explanation.surface: A refund taken on someone's behalf by a ne'er-do-well.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled good-for-nothing, like a wastrel.

clue.text: The way to a person's heart? Quite the reverse!

definitions.text: The way to a person's heart? Quite the reverse!

parts.words: The way to a person's heart? Quite the reverse!
parts.note: the phrase about the way to someone's heart is flipped: this is the way out of the heart, the great artery carrying blood away

explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leading blood away from the heart, the reverse of a way in.

clue.text: Inclined to have trouble starting and finishing

indicators.note: starting takes the opening letter of trouble

parts.note: a finishing is an ending

explanation.surface: Apt to find it hard to begin and to end things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble starting' looks like a difficulty but gives T; 'to have' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending to do something means being inclined or disposed towards it.

clue.text: Bride worried about lines is lacking in refinement

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters go round the lines
worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: L is a line, and LL lines

explanation.surface: An anxious bride fretting over her speech is rather coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bride' tempts as the definition of a wedding word, but it is the fodder for 'worried'; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-bred means badly brought up, rude and lacking good manners.

clue.text: Event in which the winners tied for victory

definitions.text: Event in which the winners tied for victory

parts.words: Event in which the winners tied for victory
parts.note: the winners are not level on points but literally bound together at the leg, running as a pair

explanation.definitionFit: In this sports-day race two runners have adjacent legs strapped together, so the winners are physically tied.
